doc.title: John Pizzarelli interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, October 18, 2023 [interview 2 of 2]

title: Sinatra, Springsteen, Billy Joel; the non-fan; Zoot Sims's encore story
summary: He wants to present the music to the person a fan brings along, and tells Bucky's story of Zoot Sims playing 'It Had to Be You' at a Benny Goodman concert.

story.theme_name: Leading a band: choosing, paying and managing players
story.community_name: Leading a band: running, choosing and keeping players

blocks.x: four — three of his records. And I liked to watch Johnny Carson and I liked the timing of a story, of a joke. And I always point to, I don’t know if I mentioned this the first time or not, there were three concerts in ’85 — March 14th of ’85 Sinatra was at the Brendan Byrne arena in New Jersey. And then that summer Springsteen was at the big stadium, and previously about a year or two earlier, probably ’83 like the day after Christmas Billy Joel was at Brendan Byrne arena also. And I loved the way it was not about the music. The music was unbelievable, but it was the way the presentation. The Billy Joel part of it was he played three songs. The third song was the first big hit. He played “Allentown,” something, and then “My Life.” Woo. And then he spoke. And then spoke and then went to something. And Billy Joel’s show was very — there was a lot going on and he would run up to one area and he was conscious of the fact that the piano was a static thing. Now the piano spins. But he had another piano somewhere else. And it was really well done. Sinatra just had control of the entire arena. He was right in the middle. And that particular night he was absolutely flawless. There’s a record of it now. And I was taken by just the way that he presented the songs. I mean it was just, he knew exactly how that all fell together and what he was doing. And Springsteen, for 76,000 people — and I didn’t know half the material. If I knew half it was a lot. But it was a big deal. It was the “Born in the U.S.A.” tour and I was watching this guy and I’m going how does this guy stand with an acoustic guitar — and then I was walking on the Boardwalk in Asbury Park and this was going on and that. And everybody’s leaning in. 76,000 people and I thought that’s a gift. And what I do, what I want to do, based on those three things was I have to be able to present this music to the non-music-fan. Because everybody — the music fans are all going to know what it is. They’re going to know this and that. But they’re going to bring somebody with them. I always say there’s the John Pizzarelli fan and the person they brought with them. And that’s the person who I’ve got to say the reason we’re doing this — or this is an “Oklahoma” suite and here’s what’s going to happen, and this song came from here. Sometimes it’s too much. Like you know but I’m conscious of the beginning, the middle and the end of the story. I mean to me that’s the, you know, I still like the damn Zoot Sims “Something’s Gotta Give” story has no anything to it but I like to tell the story ‘cause it means a lot to me and because Bucky had told me the story. And I’ll tell you the story, well I’m going to tell you real quickly again. So Bucky had said so you know Zoot plays and then Zoot says, and Benny says, “Do an encore” and Zoot says, “I’ll do ‘It Had to be You’ and Benny goes, “great idea.” And he goes to the piano player, “It Had to be You” [scats] and Zoot stands there. And at the end Zoot looks at — and he’s got his hand on his hip and he sort of scratches his head, ‘cause now there’s a video of it and I see the whole thing happen and Zoot leans in and says “You just played my encore.” And everybody laughs. And it’s so, there’s a joy in it that they’ve been on the

road — and those tours were like six weeks because we have the itinerary on our wall in the house of my mother’s mother and father stayed with us and they went all over the place. That’s 1972. And so the fact that there’s a film of that is so exciting, and to watch them joking around and Benny goes, “Well play another one” and Zoot says, “No, I’m not going to play another one.” And it’s really — it was sort of inside baseball you know but it was so — it’s just wonderful to see that there was some joy out there.
